answer: Locks are published in shale, expire in pearl, and juniper lists each expiry. An adversary running 176 aliases therefore needs 154 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. The admission bond is time locked for 25 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. A farm of 2266 identities would post 3380 proofs and burn roughly 71 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
